help.stdout:
usage: mem [-h] [--root ROOT]
           {check,index,find,search,passages,related,show,read,topics,stats,review,fetch-sources,search-eval,rename,note,import,import-recover,unify,new,remember,session-index,compact-log,signal,confirm,observe,refute,forget,triage,supersede,merge,distinct,restore,promote,memories,curate,rules,settle,project-synthesis,synthesis,terms,projects,init,history,memory,install-command,diagnostics} ...

Memory engine: search and read a store of notes.

positional arguments:
  {check,index,find,search,passages,related,show,read,topics,stats,review,fetch-sources,search-eval,rename,note,import,import-recover,unify,new,remember,session-index,compact-log,signal,confirm,observe,refute,forget,triage,supersede,merge,distinct,restore,promote,memories,curate,rules,settle,project-synthesis,synthesis,terms,projects,init,history,memory,install-command,diagnostics}
    check               validate the hub rules
    index               regenerate the index blocks in the folder READMEs
    find                list notes matching all filters
    search              rank notes by BM25 relevance to a query
    passages            print the passages of a note's local source that best
                        match
    related             list a note's links, backlinks and most similar notes
    show (read)         print chosen sections of notes
    topics              print the topic tree with note counts
    stats               print note, topic and size counts
    review              list concrete requirements due for review and notes
                        due for re-testing or re-reading
    fetch-sources       download literature note urls into .sources/
    search-eval         measure search recall on docs/search-eval.md
    rename              rename a note in its folder and rewrite the links to
                        it
    note                change a note through mem, never by editing its file
    import              copy the notes of another folder of notes into the
                        store; the source is never changed
    import-recover      roll back an interrupted import
    unify               replace several notes of one type with one, keeping
                        the others as superseded files and pointing their
                        links at it
    new                 create a note from its template
    remember            write a memory in the project or, with --global, in
                        the global folder
    session-index       print the text that opens a session: usage rules and
                        counts
    compact-log         check the handoff block of a compaction summary and
                        log counts
    signal              print the records related to a brief read from
                        standard input
    confirm             count one more observation of a memory
    observe             alias of confirm
    refute              mark a memory refuted
    forget              mark a memory forgotten
    triage              decide what a corroborated general lesson becomes
    supersede           mark OLD as superseded by NEW
    merge               add DROP's count and body to KEEP and supersede DROP
    distinct            record that two memories are different claims: the
                        queue stops pairing them
    restore             put back the text a memory had before its last
                        curation action
    promote             print a draft of a global memory from project memories
    memories            list memories, newest first
    curate              list what needs a decision: pairs, expired, frequent,
                        unconfirmed
    rules               print the rules that load at session start; --more
                        lists the rest
    settle              settle new global memories against their look-alikes
                        (verdicts from a file)
    project-synthesis   write, confirm and list the stamped parts of a
                        project's syntheses
    synthesis           create and extend syntheses, the long documents behind
                        notes
    terms               manage the terms that must not reach the global scope
    projects            the local registry of projects whose memories can be
                        searched
    init                make a folder a writable store (default: the default
                        store)
    history             the store's git history: list, init, commit
    memory              change a memory through mem, never by editing its file
    install-command     install `mem`, `mem-research` and `mem-synthesize` as
                        commands on PATH (launchers that follow the plugin)
    diagnostics         report local host configuration and observed hook
                        delivery

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --root ROOT           store folder (default: $MEM_STORE, then the config
                        file)

help confirm.stdout:
usage: mem confirm [-h] [--global] [--until YYYY-MM-DD]
                   [--source 'session ID'] [--note TEXT]
                   [--outcome {worked,failed,seen}] [--seen-on YYYY-MM-DD]
                   [--by-owner]
                   m:HANDLE

positional arguments:
  m:HANDLE

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --global              act on the global memory when the handle exists in
                        both scopes
  --until YYYY-MM-DD    also set valid_until to this date
  --source 'session ID'
                        another session shows it: add it as a source (exit 3
                        when already one)
  --note TEXT           with --source: a line added to the body
  --outcome {worked,failed,seen}
                        with --source: what that session showed about the
                        lesson (default seen)
  --seen-on YYYY-MM-DD  with --source: the day of that session (default today)
  --by-owner            the owner vouches for a transcript lesson: it is
                        established (exit 3 when already)

help curate.stdout:
usage: mem curate [-h] [--project | --global] [--notes] [--done]
                  [--new-since EPOCH] [--safe] [--from FILE]
                  [{apply}]

positional arguments:
  {apply}            apply: carry out the safe actions read from --from FILE
                     or stdin (needs --safe)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --project          the project's memories only
  --global           the global memories only
  --notes            list notes to attach to a synthesis part, and notes older
                     than their part
  --done             record today as the date of the last pass over the scopes
                     covered
  --new-since EPOCH  print the number of global memories and notes written
                     since EPOCH seconds (and since the last pass)
  --safe             with apply: only merges of equal claims and attaches the
                     part's Sources line backs
  --from FILE        with apply: the action lines (default or -: stdin)

help memory edit.stdout:
usage: mem memory edit [-h] [--claim TEXT] [--context TEXT] [--body-file PATH]
                       [--short TEXT] [--user-read] [--reworded]
                       [--reword-failed] [--topic TEXT] [--no-load |
                       --index-only | --load] [--shrink] [--owner-approved]
                       [--global]
                       m:HANDLE

positional arguments:
  m:HANDLE

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --claim TEXT      the new claim (one sentence)
  --context TEXT    the new context; an empty text removes it
  --body-file PATH  the new body; - reads standard input
  --short TEXT      the one-line rule loaded at session start; an empty text
                    removes it
  --user-read       with --short: the owner read this text, so it skips the
                    code check and carries no mark; without it the short form
                    is checked against the claim and marked as written by a
                    model
  --reworded        with --short: the automatic step wrote this text; marks
                    the lesson as reworded
  --reword-failed   alone: note that the automatic rewording gave up on the
                    last version
  --topic TEXT      one or two lowercase words; an empty text removes it
  --no-load         never load this lesson as a rule
  --index-only      never load this lesson as a rule, but count it in the
                    index line by topic
  --load            remove --no-load and --index-only
  --shrink          accept a text that drops over 20% of the words, a sentence
                    or a link
  --owner-approved  the owner agreed to a write that mentions a soft term:
                    never add it on your own
  --global          edit the global memory when the handle exists in both
                    scopes

options:

  --claim CLAIM

  --context CONTEXT
  --short TEXT          the claim as one line of at most 120 characters,
                        loaded at session start
  --user-read           with --short: the owner read this text, so it skips
                        the code check and carries no mark; without it the
                        short form is checked against the claim and marked as
                        written by a model
  --topic TEXT          one or two lowercase words that group rules
  --valid-until YYYY-MM-DD
  --source URL_OR_PATH
  --origin {web,pipeline,transcript}
                        where the claim came from when not a session: web (a
                        finding), pipeline (a pipeline's write) or transcript
                        (a lesson captured from a session transcript)
  --reach {project,general}
                        how far the lesson reaches
  --weight {light,medium,strong}
                        how much it weighs: light needs 1 session to be
                        established, medium 2, strong 3
  --outcome {worked,failed,seen}
                        what the session showed about the lesson; recorded as
                        a case of its log
  --seen-on YYYY-MM-DD  the day of the session, when it is not today
  --global
  --force               write even when a memory has the same claim
  --owner-approved      the owner agreed to a write that mentions a soft term:
                        never add it on your own
